words.gloss: altered, abnormal (vikṛta); disease (vyādhi); concerning knowledge, to be known (vijñānīya)

hindi: अब इसलिए हम विकृत व्याधियों के ज्ञान से सम्बन्धित अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the chapter on the knowledge of abnormal (vikṛta) diseases.
notes: Opening formula (atha ataḥ ... vyākhyāsyāmaḥ). 'Vikṛtavyādhivijñānīya' is the chapter title; 'vikṛta' is rendered literally ('altered, abnormal'). The content of the chapter (signs of fatal disease) is not stated in this line and is not imported. Printed -yamadhyāyaṃ is simply -yam adhyāyam run together.

words.gloss: piplu (mole; probable); vyaṅga (blemish, a dark patch of the skin; probable); line (lekhā); tilakālaka (black specks on the skin; probable)
of one who is wasting away
eyelid (vartman); nose (nāsikā); either of the two (anyatara); swelling (śvayathu)
throat; mouth; anus; inflammation, literally ripening (pāka)
āmāśaya and pakvāśaya (the receptacles of raw and of cooked food; probably the stomach and the large intestine); one of the two (anyatara)

hindi: जिसकी व्याधि सब हेतुओं, पूर्वरूपों और रूपों के साथ, अपने-अपने अनुसार, अत्यधिक मात्रा में उत्पन्न होती है; या जिस रोगी के मुख पर शीघ्र पिप्लु यानी सम्भवतः मस्से, व्यंग यानी सम्भवतः त्वचा के काले धब्बे, रेखाएँ और तिलकालक यानी सम्भवतः त्वचा के काले कण हैं, या नाखूनों और दाँतों पर पुष्प यानी फूल हैं, या पेट पर अनेक रंगों की सिराएँ यानी नसें हैं; जिसके सूखते हुए आँखों पर उपदेह यानी लेप है, पलक या नाक में से किसी एक की सूजन है, या पलक का झड़ना है; जिसके क्षीण होने पर भूख या प्यास बहुत से मनोहर अन्न और पानों से भी शान्त नहीं होती; जिससे झाग सहित रक्त बहाया जाता है, कुक्षि यानी पेट के पार्श्व में शूल यानी पीड़ा और छाती की भी, या; जिसका श्लेष्मा नीला, पीला और लाल है और बार-बार; जिसके गले का तीव्र अवमर्द यानी कुचला जाना, जीभ का सूखना, और कण्ठ, मुख तथा गुदा का पाक यानी पकना है; जिसके आमाशय यानी सम्भवतः जठर से उठी हुई परिकर्तिका यानी काटने वाली पीड़ा, अत्यन्त प्यास और मल का टूटना है; जिसके पक्वाशय यानी सम्भवतः बड़ी आँत से उठी हुई परिकर्तिका, अत्यन्त प्यास और अत्यधिक गुदग्रह यानी गुदा की जकड़न है; जिसके आमाशय या पक्वाशय में से किसी एक का आश्रय लेकर और संज्ञा यानी चेतना को नष्ट करके वायु कण्ठ में घुरघुरक यानी घुरघुर की आवाज़ करता है; जिसके क्षीण होने पर प्यास की वृद्धि और हृदय में शूल है, तथा हिचकी और रक्तातिसार यानी खूनी दस्त, या आध्मान यानी अफारा और अतिसार है, और जो बहुत प्यासा है, वह परासु है, यानी जिसके प्राण चले गए हैं।
english: He whose disease arises with all its causes, premonitory signs (prāgrūpa) and signs (rūpa), each in its own way, to excess; or a sick man in whom quickly there are, on the face, moles (piplu, probably), blemishes (vyaṅga, probably), lines (lekhā) and tilakālaka (black specks of the skin, probably), or, on the nails and teeth, flowers (puṣpa), or, on the belly, veins (sirā) of various colours; he who, while wasting away, has a coating on the eyes (netra-upadeha), a swelling of either the eyelid or the nose, or a drooping of the eyelid; he who, being wasted, has hunger or thirst that is not allayed even by many agreeable foods and drinks; he from whom frothy blood is discharged, with pain in the flank and (pain) of the chest, or; he whose phlegm (śleṣman) is blue, yellow and red, and repeatedly so; he who has a strong crushing of the neck, dryness of the tongue, and inflammation (pāka, literally 'ripening') of the throat, mouth and anus; he who has parikartikā (cutting pain) arising in the āmāśaya (probably the stomach), excessive thirst and breaking of the stool; he who has parikartikā arising in the pakvāśaya (probably the large intestine), excessive thirst and an excessive grasp of the anus (gudagraha); he in whom wind (vāyu), having resorted to either the āmāśaya or the pakvāśaya and having destroyed consciousness (saṃjñā), makes a gurgling sound (ghurghuraka) in the throat; he who, wasted, has increase of thirst and pain in the heart, and likewise hiccup and bloody diarrhoea, or bloating and diarrhoea, and who is greatly thirsty: he is parāsu (one whose life-breaths are gone).

text_flags.why: possible: 'savair' is not a word; the r of 'sarvaiḥ' has dropped
possible: the hiatus 'ca uraso' is printed run together (Devanagari चउरसो); the intended words are ca urasaḥ
possible: 'kṣaṇisya' is not a word; 'kṣīṇasya' (of the wasted one) matches the same phrase earlier in the unit
possible: printed 'satṛṣṇo sa' has o before s, which is not regular sandhi; satṛṣṇaḥ saḥ (thirsty, he) is meant

notes: One long prose sentence of alternative signs, each introduced by 'yasya' ('of whom/whose'); the closing 'sa parāsuḥ iti' gives the conclusion for each. Copula understood in the verbless clauses (shown as 'has' or 'there are'). The closing 'iti' is not translated. 'parāsu' = one whose life-breaths (asu) have gone; the line itself does not say 'doomed to die', so no more is added (the chapter appears to list fatal signs, but that is not stated here). Printed 'vāyasyāśu' = vā yasya āśu; 'cauraso' = ca urasaḥ (hiatus printed joined; 'śūla' of the chest is understood from kukṣiśūlam). 'puṣpa' = flowers, read literally; later medicine uses it for white spots on the nails (not adopted). tilakālaka, piplu and vyaṅga are skin marks (probable identifications). 'bahuśaḥ' is read as 'repeatedly'. 'netropadeha' = coating (smearing) on the eyes. 'śakṛdbheda' = breaking of the stool (probably loose stool). 'gudagraha' = grasp of the anus. 'āmapakvāśayānyataram' is read as 'one of the two, āmāśaya or pakvāśaya'. 'hidhmā-raktātisārau' and 'ādhmāna-atīsārau' are dual dvandvas (two members each). The avagraha printed after -ā (parikartikā'ti-) is a print habit. 'kṣaṇisya' is read as kṣīṇasya (flagged).

hindi: और इस विषय में है।
english: And here there is.
notes: Lead-in formula 'bhavati ca atra' ('and here there is ...'); nothing is supplied after it because the Sanskrit states no object. GROUPING: this unit is a formula that appears to introduce the verse units that follow (unit 4 onward).

hindi: बलवान्, गहरा और दीर्घरात्रिक यानी लम्बी रातों वाला ज्वर यानी बुखार मारता है।
english: A fever (jvara) that is strong, deep (gambhīra) and long-lasting (dīrgharātrika, literally 'of long nights') kills.
notes: The verb nihanti has no object in this line; accusative objects follow in the next units, so the sentence is left as the Sanskrit gives it. 'dīrgharātrika' is literally 'having long nights' (lasting many days).

words.gloss: destroyed (hata); fire (anala; probably the digestive fire)

hindi: प्रलाप यानी बड़बड़ाहट, भ्रम यानी चक्कर और श्वास यानी साँस फूलने से युक्त; क्षीण, सूजे हुए, और जिसकी अग्नि यानी सम्भवतः पाचन की अग्नि नष्ट हो गई है उसको।
english: Accompanied by delirium (pralāpa), giddiness (bhrama) and breathlessness (śvāsa); the one who is wasted, swollen, whose fire (anala, probably the digestive fire) is destroyed.
notes: The first word is nominative and agrees with jvaraḥ of unit 4; the other three words are accusative, the objects of nihanti in unit 4 (the verb is carried over, none is supplied). 'anala' = fire, probably the digestive fire (probable).

hindi: जो कृश नहीं है, जिसकी वाणी अटकती है, लाल आँखों वाले और हृदय में शूल यानी पीड़ा वाले को।
english: The one who is not emaciated (akṣāma), whose speech is faltering (sakta-vacana, literally 'speech stuck'), who is red-eyed and has pain in the heart (hṛd).

text_flags.why: possible: 'not emaciated' sits oddly beside kṣīṇam (wasted) in unit 5; 'kṣāmam' (emaciated, or of weak voice) may be meant. Not adopted: the printed word is a valid word and is translated as printed.

notes: Accusative objects continue from unit 4/5 (verb carried over). akṣāma is translated as printed ('not emaciated'); its fit beside 'kṣīṇam' is doubtful, hence the flag and medium confidence. sakta = clinging or stuck, so sakta-vacana is faltering or halting speech.

hindi: संशुष्क कास यानी अत्यन्त सूखी खाँसी, जो पूर्वाह्न में या अपराह्न में भी हो।
english: A very dry cough (saṃśuṣka-kāsa) that may occur in the forenoon or even in the afternoon.
notes: Fresh nominative subject; it is not said in this line what it does (the sentence is a list of ominous signs begun in unit 4).

hindi: बल और मांस से रहित का, श्लेष्मकास यानी कफ की खाँसी से युक्त।
english: Of one deprived of strength and flesh, accompanied by phlegm-cough (śleṣma-kāsa).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue unit 7. Whether 'samanvitaḥ' (nominative) qualifies the dry cough of unit 7 or the person is not decided by the Sanskrit; both are shown literally. śleṣma-kāsa = cough with phlegm (Kapha cough).

hindi: रक्तपित्त यानी सम्भवतः रक्तस्राव का रोग, बहुत लाल, काला, इन्द्रधनुष की आभा वाला।
english: Raktapitta (a bleeding disorder, probably), very red, black, with the lustre of the rainbow (Indra's bow).

text_flags.why: 'idra' is not a word; the anusvāra of 'indra' has dropped (the sense 'rainbow' is certain)

notes: raktapitta = disorder of bleeding from the body (probable); the term is kept. 'bhṛśam' is read with 'raktam' ('very red'); it could also be a separate adverb. The adjectives describe the discharged blood, which is not named in this line.

hindi: ताँबे के रंग का, हल्दी के रंग का, हरा और लाल रूप दिखाए।
english: It should show a copper-coloured, turmeric-coloured, green and red (rakta) appearance (rūpa).
notes: 'raktam' is read as the colour 'red' in a list of colours; it could also be the noun 'blood' (so 'show blood in a copper-coloured, turmeric-coloured, green appearance'). The subject of darśayet is not stated (continuing raktapitta of unit 9; GROUPING: appears to continue unit 9).

words.gloss: hair (roma); pit, pore (kūpa); spread forth, issued (pravisṛta)

hindi: रोमकूप यानी रोमछिद्रों से निकला हुआ; कण्ठ, मुख और हृदय में अस्पष्ट शब्द सजत, अनुमानित पाठ पर।
english: Issued through the hair-pits (roma-kūpa); an unclear word (printed sajataṃ) in the throat, mouth and heart (hṛdaya), on a conjectural reading.

text_flags.why: possible: 'sajata' is not a word as printed; 'saṃjātam' (arisen) or 'saktam' (clinging) are the nearest candidates. Neither is adopted; the word stays unclear.

notes: The printed word 'sajataṃ' is not restorable with certainty and is left unclear (candidates only in the flag). GROUPING: appears to continue units 9-10. 'pravisṛta' = spread forth, issued.

hindi: वस्त्र का रंगना, सड़ा हुआ, वेग वाला और बहुत अधिक भी।
english: Staining of clothing; putrid (pūti), forceful and also very abundant.
notes: Subject not stated; GROUPING: appears to continue units 9-11 (the discharge described there). 'pūti' is rendered 'putrid' (it may include foul smell).

words.gloss: unclear (the stem chard- 'vomit' is visible but the form is doubtful)
pāṇḍu (anaemia with pallor; standard); fever (jvara); vomiting (chardi); cough (kāsa); swelling (śopha); having diarrhoea (atisārin)

hindi: अस्पष्ट शब्द छर्द्दं; पाण्डु यानी रक्ताल्पता, ज्वर, उल्टी, खाँसी, सूजन और अतिसार वाले को, अनुमानित पाठ पर।
english: An unclear word (printed charddaṃ); the one who has pāṇḍu (anaemia with pallor), fever (jvara), vomiting (chardi), cough (kāsa), swelling (śopha) and diarrhoea (atisāra), on a conjectural reading.

text_flags.suggest: chardiṃ or another form of chard- (vomiting)
text_flags.why: possible: the form 'charddaṃ' is not clear and duplicates 'chardi' inside the next word; left unclear in the translation

notes: Accusative object (verb carried over from unit 4). Printed doubled 'dd' in chardi is a spelling habit and is written 'chardi' in the words. The first word is left unclear because its form is doubtful.

words.gloss: fever (jvara); vomiting (chardi); thirst (tṛṣṇā); diarrhoea (atīsāra); having swelling (śophin)

hindi: खाँसी यानी कास और साँस फूलना यानी श्वास; ज्वर यानी बुखार, उल्टी, प्यास, अतिसार यानी दस्त और सूजन वाले को।
english: Cough and breathlessness (kāsa and śvāsa); the one with fever (jvara), vomiting (chardi), thirst (tṛṣṇā), diarrhoea (atīsāra) and swelling.
notes: Elliptical: nominative dual subject, accusative object, verb (nihanti) carried over from unit 4 and not supplied. Printed 'atīsāra' (long ī) is kept as printed.

words.gloss: side (pārśva); pain (ruj); distension (ānāha); blood (rakta); vomiting (chardi); not (a); burning heat, distress (saṃtāpin)

hindi: यक्ष्मन् यानी सम्भवतः क्षय रोग; पार्श्व में पीड़ा, आनाह यानी पेट के तनाव, रक्त की उल्टी वाले और ताप से रहित को।
english: Yakṣman (consumption, probably tuberculosis); the one with pain in the side, distension (ānāha), vomiting of blood, and without burning heat (asaṃtāpin).
notes: Elliptical (verb carried over). The last element 'a-saṃtāpin' is read literally as 'without burning heat/distress'; its sense in a list of ominous signs is not clear, hence medium confidence. ānāha = distension.

hindi: उल्टी यानी छर्दि, वेगवती, मूत्र और मल की गन्ध वाली, चन्द्रिका सहित; चन्द्रिका यानी चाँदनी, जिसका यहाँ अर्थ अस्पष्ट है।
english: Vomiting (chardi), forceful, smelling of urine and faeces, with candrikā (literally 'moonlight'; its sense here is uncertain).
notes: 'candrikā' is literally moonlight (or moon-like marks); what it names here is not stated, so no interpretation is added. Printed doubled 'dd' in chardi normalised.

words.gloss: with asra (sa-asra; asra = blood or tears)

hindi: असरा सहित अर्थात् रक्त या आँसू सहित; अस्पष्ट समास विट्पूयरुक्कासश्वासवत्य; अस्पष्ट शब्द गुंषिणो; अनुमानित पाठ पर।
english: With asra (blood, or tears); an unclear compound (printed viṭpūyarukkāsaśvāsavatya); an unclear word (printed guṃṣiṇo); on a conjectural reading.

text_flags.why: possible: 'guṃṣiṇo' is not a word; 'yakṣmiṇaḥ' (of consumptives) is a conceivable but unproven correction. Not adopted.
possible: the ending '-vatya' does not parse; the compound is left unsplit and untranslated

notes: Damaged print. Visible parts of the long compound are viṭ (faeces), pūya (pus), ruj (pain), kāsa (cough), śvāsa (breath), but the ending is not clear, so it is not translated in part. 'sāsra' is read as sa-asra; asra can mean blood or tear. GROUPING: appears to continue the list of unit 15-16 (yakṣman), not certain.

hindi: तृष्णा यानी प्यास; दूसरे रोगों से क्षीण किए गए, बाहर निकली जीभ वाले और अचेत को।
english: Thirst (tṛṣṇā); the one worn down by other ailments, with the tongue outside, unconscious.
notes: Elliptical (verb carried over). The avagraha printed after -ā (tṛṣṇā'nya-) is a print habit. 'bahir-jihva' = tongue outside (protruding).

words.gloss: madātyaya (ailment from intoxicating drink, an alcohol-related disorder; probable)

hindi: मदात्यय यानी सम्भवतः मद्य से उत्पन्न रोग; अत्यन्त शीत से पीड़ित, क्षीण और तेल की चमक वाले मुख वाले को।
english: Madātyaya (an ailment from intoxicating drink, probably an alcohol-related disorder); the one afflicted by great cold, wasted, whose face has the lustre of oil.
notes: Elliptical (verb carried over). The print has a dropped avagraha after -o (madātyayo 'ti-) which is regular sandhi here (madātyayaḥ ati).

words.gloss: hand (pāṇi); foot (pad); navel (nābhi); anus (guda); testicle (muṣka); mouth (āsya); having swelling (śophin)

hindi: अर्श यानी बवासीर; हाथ, पैर, नाभि, गुदा, मुष्क यानी अण्डकोष और मुख में सूजन वाले को।
english: Arśas (haemorrhoids, piles); the one with swelling of the hands, feet, navel, anus, testicles (muṣka) and mouth.

text_flags.why: anusvāra dropped: the neuter plural of arśas is arśāṃsi

notes: Elliptical (verb carried over). 'pannābhi' is pad + nābhi (regular sandhi). āsya = mouth (also 'face').

words.gloss: heart (hṛd); side (pārśva); limb, body part (aṅga); pain (ruj); vomiting (chardi); anus (pāyu); inflammation, literally ripening (pāka); fever (jvara); afflicted (ātura)

hindi: हृदय, पार्श्व और अंग की पीड़ा, उल्टी, गुदा के पाक यानी पकने और ज्वर से पीड़ित को।
english: The one afflicted by pain in the heart, side and limbs, vomiting, inflammation (pāka, literally 'ripening') of the anus, and fever.
notes: Elliptical (verb carried over; GROUPING: unit 21 appears to complete the object begun in unit 20, arśas). The compound can also be read as 'pain of heart, side and limb' in one group, as here.

words.gloss: liver (yakṛt); lump (piṇḍa); flesh, meat (māṃsa); washing (dhāvana); dark blue-black (mecaka)

hindi: अतिसार यानी दस्त, यकृत के पिण्डों, मांस के धोवन और गहरे नीले-काले से।
english: Diarrhoea (atīsāra), with liver-lumps (yakṛt-piṇḍa), meat-washings (māṃsa-dhāvana) and dark (mecaka) ones.
notes: The instrumental plurals are completed by 'tulyaḥ' in unit 23 (similar to); the construction is left as printed. 'mecaka' = dark blue-black (also peacock-coloured); read as an adjective with an unstated noun, shown as '(ones)'. GROUPING: appears to continue in unit 23-24.

words.gloss: oil (taila); ghee (ghṛta); milk (kṣīra); curd (dadhi); marrow (majjā); fat (vasā); fermented liquor (āsava)

hindi: तेल, घी, दूध, दही, मज्जा, वसा और आसव यानी किण्वित पेय के समान।
english: Similar to oil, ghee, milk, curd, marrow, fat (vasā) and āsava (a fermented liquor).
notes: Continues unit 22 (diarrhoea). 'majja' in a compound is the stem of majjā or majjan; 'marrow' in this body context. GROUPING: appears to continue unit 22 and run on into unit 24.

words.gloss: first part of mastuluṅga (brain-matter; probable), printed apart from luṅga
second part of mastuluṅga; soot (maṣī); pus (pūya); veśavāra (a preparation of minced meat; standard); water (ambu); honey (mākṣika)

hindi: मस्तुलुंग यानी सम्भवतः मस्तिष्क का पदार्थ, मषी यानी कालिख, पूय यानी मवाद, वेशवार यानी पिसे हुए मांस की बनी तैयारी, जल और शहद से, अनुमानित पाठ पर।
english: With mastuluṅga (brain-matter, probably), soot (maṣī), pus (pūya), veśavāra (a preparation of minced meat), water and honey, on a conjectural reading.

text_flags.why: possible: a space has fallen inside the word 'mastuluṅga' (brain). Alternative: mastu (whey) and luṅga (citron) as two words. The joined reading is adopted and marked conjectural in the translations.
possible: 'raṃbu' has a stray anusvāra for 'rāmbu' (veśavāra + ambu); 'vesavāra' is spelled with s for ś

notes: Continues the list of units 22-23. The word-space in 'mastu luṃga' is read as an error for mastuluṅga (brain), which is a conjecture; hence the conjectural mark. 'veśavāra' = a preparation of boneless minced meat (standard, name kept).

words.gloss: red (rakta); black (asita); unctuous (snigdha); putrid (pūti); clear (accha); thick, dense (ghana); pain, feeling (vedana)

hindi: अति, लाल, काला, चिकना, सड़ा हुआ, स्वच्छ, घना, पीड़ा वाला।
english: Very (ati) red, black, unctuous (snigdha), putrid (pūti), clear (accha), thick (ghana), with pain (vedana).
notes: 'ati' is printed apart and is kept as a separate adverb; it could also be the first member of a compound with 'rakta'. The noun described is not stated (the stool, continuing units 22-24, appears likely). 'ghana-vedana' could also be 'with dense (intense) pain'.

hindi: चितकबरा; अस्पष्ट शब्द प्रस्रवन्धात्त्रिष्पूरीषो; अथवा बहुत अधिक मल वाला; अनुमानित पाठ पर।
english: Mottled (karbura); an unclear word (printed prasravandhāttriṣpūrīṣo); or else with excessive faeces (ati-viṭ); on a conjectural reading.

text_flags.why: possible: 'dhāttriṣ' does not parse; 'triṣ' may be 'niṣ' (nasal/tra confusion), giving niṣpūrīṣaḥ (without faeces), which would pair with 'ati-viṭ' (with much faeces). Not adopted; left unclear.

notes: Damaged print. The visible word 'prasravan' (flowing) is joined to the unclear part by sandhi, so the whole stretch is left unsplit and unclear. The avagraha after -ā in 'athavā'ti-' is a print habit.

hindi: तन्तुओं वाला, मषिका यानी कालिख के कण से आक्रान्त, अस्पष्ट शब्द राजैर्मांसेंद्रकैर् से युक्त; अनुमानित पाठ पर।
english: Fibrous (tantumat), overspread (ākrānta) with soot-specks (maṣikā), joined with unclear words (printed rājair māṃseṃdrakair); on a conjectural reading.

text_flags.why: possible: s for ṣ (the print confuses these elsewhere)
possible: 'rājair' and 'māṃseṃdrakair' do not give a sure sense; left unclear

notes: Continues the description of the stool (units 22-26). 'maṣikā' is read as soot or black specks; the s/ṣ spelling is a print habit. The last two words are not restorable and are left unclear.

hindi: शीर्ण गुदा की वलि यानी तह वाले, मुक्त नाल यानी छूटे हुए डंठल वाले और जोड़ों व हड्डियों में शूल यानी पीड़ा वाले को, अनुमानित पाठ पर।
english: The one whose folds (vali) of the anus are withered, whose stalk (nāla) is released (its sense here is uncertain), who has pain in the joints and bones; on a conjectural reading.

text_flags.why: possible: 'vāli' (long ā) may be 'vali' (fold); the print interchanges v and b elsewhere and vowel lengths are loose. Adopted conjecturally.

notes: Elliptical (verb carried over). 'nāla' = stalk; what is meant (perhaps a part of the anus or rectum) is not stated, so nothing is added.

hindi: गुदा के खिसकने यानी निकल आने वाले, बल से क्षीण को; अस्पष्ट शब्द अन्नेवोपवेशयन्; अनुमानित पाठ पर।
english: The one with a prolapsed anus (srasta-pāyu), wasted in strength; an unclear word (printed annevopaveśayan); on a conjectural reading.

text_flags.suggest: annaṃ vā upaveśayan or anne vā upaveśayan
text_flags.why: possible: both parse as 'anna(m) vā upaveśayan' but the sense of upaveśayan ('causing to sit') is not clear here. Left unclear.

notes: The last word is left unclear. srasta-pāyu = slipped anus (prolapse of the anus or rectum, probable). GROUPING: appears to continue the object list of units 26-28.

words.gloss: fever (jvara); vomiting (chardi); burning (dāha); distension (ānāha); having pravāhikā (flux with straining, dysentery; probable)

hindi: प्यास सहित, खाँसी, ज्वर, उल्टी, दाह यानी जलन, आनाह यानी पेट के तनाव और प्रवाहिका यानी सम्भवतः मरोड़ के साथ पेचिश वाला; अनुमानित पाठ पर।
english: With thirst, cough, fever, vomiting, burning (dāha), distension (ānāha) and pravāhikā (flux with straining, probably dysentery); on a conjectural reading.

text_flags.suggest: satṛṭ kāsa (and the next token then begins jvara-)
text_flags.why: possible: 'satṛṭkā majvara-' does not parse; 'sa' and 'ma' are confused in this print, so the next word likely begins 'jvara' and 'kāsa' (cough) is meant. Syllable count (16) is the same either way. Adopted conjecturally.

notes: Nominative adjectives for the stool/diarrhoea of units 22-29. The emendation moves a letter across the token boundary, so the tokens are given as printed and the words as emended. pravāhikā is flux with straining (probable).

hindi: अश्मरी यानी मूत्र की पथरी; सूजे हुए वृषणों वाले, रुके हुए मूत्र वाले और पीड़ा से पीड़ित को।
english: Aśmarī (urinary stone); the one with swollen testicles, with obstructed urine, afflicted by pain.
notes: Elliptical (verb carried over from unit 4).

words.gloss: meha (prameha, a urinary disorder, probably the diabetes-type; probable)
pricking pain (tud); burning (dāha); boils (piṭakā); flesh (māṃsa); decay (kotha); having diarrhoea (atisārin)

hindi: मेह यानी प्रमेह, सम्भवतः मधुमेह वाला रूप; चुभने वाली पीड़ा, दाह यानी जलन, पिटिका यानी फुंसियों, मांस के सड़ने और अतिसार यानी दस्त वाले को।
english: Meha (prameha, a urinary disorder, probably the diabetes-type); the one with pricking pain (tud), burning, boils (piṭakā), decay of flesh and diarrhoea.

text_flags.why: possible: 'tuddvāha' has a stray v; 'tud-dāha' (pricking pain, burning) is meant

notes: Elliptical (verb carried over). meha is the general urinary disorder, here read as prameha, probably the diabetes-type (probable). Printed 'dd' in tuddāha: tud + dāha.

words.gloss: vital spot (marma); heart (hṛd); back (pṛṣṭha); breast (stana); shoulder (aṃsa); anus (guda); head (mūrdhan); situated in (-ga)

hindi: पिटिकाएँ यानी फुंसियाँ, मर्म, हृदय, पीठ, स्तन, कन्धे, गुदा और सिर में स्थित, अनुमानित पाठ पर।
english: Boils (piṭikā) situated in the vital spots (marma), heart, back, breast, shoulder, anus and head; on a conjectural reading.

text_flags.why: possible: 'hat' for 'hṛt' (heart); the ṛ-sign is dropped. Adopted conjecturally.

notes: The final visarga of piṭikāḥ is regular sandhi before m. GROUPING: appears to continue in unit 34 ('or situated in the joints, feet or hands'). marma is a doctrinal term and is kept.

words.gloss: having prameha (prameha, a urinary disorder; probable)

hindi: जोड़ों, पैरों या हाथों में स्थित; मन्द उत्साह वाले और प्रमेह यानी मूत्र के रोग वाले को।
english: (Boils) situated in the joints, feet or hands; the one of low energy (manda-utsāha) who has prameha (a urinary disorder).

text_flags.why: possible: final anusvāra dropped in 'pramehiṇa'; an accusative is expected like the neighbouring objects

notes: Continues unit 33. The 'or' (vā) follows the place compound and is read as distributive. The unstated noun 'boils' is shown in brackets in English only.

words.gloss: flesh (māṃsa); decay (saṃkotha); burning (dāha); thirst (tṛṣṇā); intoxication (mada); fever (jvara)

hindi: और सब, मांस के सड़ने, दाह यानी जलन, प्यास, मद यानी नशा और ज्वर से।
english: And all, with decay of flesh (māṃsa-saṃkotha), burning (dāha), thirst (tṛṣṇā), intoxication (mada) and fever (jvara).
notes: Continues units 32-34. 'sarvam' ('all') is left as printed; what it refers to is not stated. GROUPING: appears to continue unit 34.

words.gloss: visarpa (erysipelas, a spreading skin inflammation; probable); vital spot (marma); obstruction (saṃrodha); hiccup (hidhmā); breathlessness (śvāsa); giddiness (bhrama); fatigue (klama)

hindi: विसर्प यानी सम्भवतः त्वचा का फैलने वाला शोथ, मर्म के संरोध यानी रुकावट, हिचकी, श्वास यानी साँस फूलना, चक्कर और थकावट से।
english: With visarpa (erysipelas, a spreading skin inflammation, probably), obstruction of the vital spots (marma-saṃrodha), hiccup (hidhmā), breathlessness (śvāsa), giddiness (bhrama) and fatigue (klama).
notes: Continues unit 35 (instrumental list). marma-saṃrodha is read as 'obstruction of the marmas'; marma is kept as a doctrinal term.

words.gloss: gulma (an abdominal lump or swelling; probable)

hindi: गुल्म यानी सम्भवतः पेट की गाँठ, चौड़े घेरे वाला, घना, कछुए के समान ऊँचा उठा हुआ; अनुमानित पाठ पर।
english: Gulma (an abdominal lump, probably), broad in girth, dense (ghana), raised like a tortoise; on a conjectural reading.

text_flags.why: possible: 'kūrmaiva' would be kūrma + eva ('the tortoise itself'), which does not fit; 'kūrma iva' (like a tortoise) gives kūrmeva. Adopted conjecturally.

notes: A fresh subject (gulma) described by adjectives; the verb is not stated.

words.gloss: fever (jvara); vomiting (chardi); hiccup (hidhmā); bloating (ādhmāna); pain (ruj); accompanied (anvita)

hindi: सिराओं यानी नसों से बँधा हुआ, ज्वर, उल्टी, हिचकी, आध्मान यानी अफारा और पीड़ा से युक्त।
english: Bound by sirās (veins), accompanied by fever, vomiting, hiccup, bloating (ādhmāna) and pain.
notes: Continues the description of the gulma of unit 37 (nominative). The avagraha after -ā (hidhmā'dhmāna) is a print habit. sirā = vein or vessel (probable).

words.gloss: cough (kāsa); pīnasa (chronic nasal catarrh; probable); nausea (hṛllāsa); breathlessness (śvāsa); diarrhoea (atīsāra); swelling (śopha); having (-vat)

hindi: खाँसी, पीनस यानी सम्भवतः पुराना जुकाम, हृल्लास यानी मिचली, श्वास यानी साँस फूलना, अतिसार यानी दस्त और सूजन वाला।
english: Having cough, pīnasa (chronic nasal catarrh, probably), nausea (hṛllāsa), breathlessness, diarrhoea (atīsāra) and swelling.
notes: Nominative continuing units 37-38 (the gulma).

words.gloss: faeces (viṭ); urine (mūtra); retention (saṃgraha); breathlessness (śvāsa); swelling (śopha); hiccup (hidhmā); fever (jvara); giddiness (bhrama)

hindi: मल और मूत्र के संग्रह यानी रुकने, श्वास यानी साँस फूलने, सूजन, हिचकी, ज्वर और चक्कर से।
english: With retention (saṃgraha) of faeces and urine, breathlessness, swelling, hiccup, fever and giddiness.
notes: Instrumental list continuing 38-39. GROUPING: appears to continue into unit 41 ('jaṭharam ... hanti').

words.gloss: jaṭhara (belly; here probably the belly disorder, an ascites-type; probable)

hindi: और मूर्च्छा यानी बेहोशी, उल्टी तथा अतिसार यानी दस्त के साथ जठर यानी पेट, यहाँ सम्भवतः पेट का रोग, दुर्बल को मारता है।
english: And with fainting (mūrcchā), vomiting and diarrhoea, jaṭhara (belly; here probably the belly disorder, an ascites-type) kills the weak (one).
notes: Here the verb hanti ('kills') is stated, matching nihanti of unit 4. 'jaṭhara' is the belly; read as the disease of the belly in this list of fatal conditions (probable). 'durbalam' is shown as 'the weak (one)'. GROUPING: appears to complete the sentence run of units 39-40.
